script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

Title: FRESH START

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

CHEF OLIVER, mid-30s, passionate chef, enters, tired after a long night at his restaurant. He rubs his eyes and orders a coffee.

BARISTA, 20s, friendly young woman, serves him a steaming cup.

BARISTA
(smiling)
You're up early today, Chef.

CHEF OLIVER
(sighs)
Yes, I've got a lot on my plate.

Suddenly, a SALESMAN enters, wearing a neon-colored suit. He carries a folder under his arm.

SALESMAN
(brightly)
Good morning! Are you in need of a new commercial refrigerator for your restaurant?

CHEF OLIVER
(sternly)
Not today, thank you.

SALESMAN
(unfazed)
Well, if you change your mind, just give me a call!

CHEF OLIVER rolls his eyes and takes a sip of his coffee. The Salesman exits.

INT. RESTAURANT KITCHEN - DAY

CHEF OLIVER walks into his kitchen, where his team is preparing lunch. He looks overwhelmed.

ASSISTANT CHEF
(concerned)
Hey, Chef, what's going on? You look exhausted.

CHEF OLIVER
(frustrated)
I've got three major events coming up at the restaurant, and all my suppliers have let me down. I need to find new ones quickly, or I'll have to cancel the events.

ASSISTANT CHEF
(sympathetic)
That's a lot of pressure. Have you tried reaching out to the farmers' market?

CHEF OLIVER
(shaking his head)
I've been there before. They don't have the quantities I need.

Suddenly, the door opens, and in walks JESSICA, a young woman with a big smile on her face. She carries a basket of fresh produce.

JESSICA
(excited)
Hey, Chef Oliver! I heard you were in a bit of a bind. I've got some fresh produce that might help!

CHEF OLIVER
(surprised)
Really? That would be amazing!

INT. RESTAURANT - NIGHT

CHEF OLIVER and JESSICA are talking in the restaurant, surrounded by the vibrant display of fresh produce.

JESSICA
(cheerfully)
So, how did you get into cooking, Chef?

CHEF OLIVER
(wistfully)
It's always been a passion of mine. But it wasn't until I had a falling out with my mentor that I really dedicated myself to it.

JESSICA
(sympathetic)
Oh no, what happened?

CHEF OLIVER
(pauses)
We had a disagreement over the direction of the restaurant. I wanted to focus on organic, locally-sourced ingredients, while he saw that as a financial risk. We argued, and I left, determined to prove him wrong.

JESSICA
(nods)
And have you?

CHEF OLIVER
(smiling)
Yes, I have. But I've also come to realize that holding a grudge wasn't worth it. I'd like to reach out to him and mend our relationship.

JESSICA
(encouraging)
That's great, Chef. Forgiveness is a powerful thing.

INT. CHEF OLIVER'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

CHEF OLIVER sits at his kitchen table, holding an old photograph of himself and his mentor. He looks thoughtful.

Suddenly, he picks up the phone and dials a number.

CHEF OLIVER
(voice trembling)
Hello, this is Oliver. I know it's been a long time, and I want to apologize for the way things ended between us. I was young and stubborn, and I let my emotions get the best of me. I'd like to meet and talk things over. What do you say?

There's a pause on the other end of the line.

MENTOR
(surprised)
Oliver? Is this a joke?

CHEF OLIVER
(serious)
No, it's not. I've come to realize that holding a grudge wasn't worth it. I'd like to make things right between us.

MENTOR
(pauses)
Alright, Oliver. I'll meet you tomorrow at the park.

CHEF OLIVER smiles, grateful for the opportunity to make amends.

INT. PARK - DAY

CHEF OLIVER and his mentor, now older and wiser, sit on a bench in the park, surrounded by the beauty of nature.

MENTOR
(looking at Oliver)
You've come a long way, Oliver. I'm proud of you.

CHEF OLIVER
(smiling)
Thank you, mentor. I couldn't have done it without your guidance.

They share a moment of silence, the weight of their past disagreement lifted.

MENTOR
(smiling)
I'm glad we've found our way back to each other.

CHEF OLIVER
(grateful)
Me too.

INT. RESTAURANT - NIGHT

CHEF OLIVER stands in the kitchen, surrounded by his team, who are preparing for the evening's events. He looks content.

ASSISTANT CHEF
(smiling)
You look happier today, Chef.

CHEF OLIVER
(smiling back)
I am. I've learned that forgiveness is a powerful thing.

JESSICA enters the kitchen, carrying a tray of fresh produce.

JESSICA
(smiling)
I see you've made things right with your mentor.

CHEF OLIVER
(nods)
Yes, I have. And I couldn't have done it without your help.

They share a warm smile, knowing that forgiveness has the power to bring people together.

FADE OUT.
